answer.rationale: Only memory_57 explicitly ties an intervention to 'qualified revenue' alongside evidence of no retention harm, making it the strongest support for the sustainable-revenue objective. memory_44 at least references 'pipeline quality,' a reasonable proxy for qualified revenue, so it gets moderate support. memory_73 mentions 'revenue lift' but omits any retention/sustainability data and promotional pricing is a known risk to long-term margin and account quality, so it's weakly supported. memory_31, memory_86, and memory_91 all describe improvements in top-of-funnel process metrics (activation, onboarding completion, week-one engagement) with no stated linkage to revenue, retention, deal quality, or downstream conversion — they are proxies at best. Among these, memory_91 is the weakest: its language ('nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action') is the vaguest, offers no quantified lift, no durability claim, and no mechanism connecting the nudge to any revenue-relevant outcome, making it the least supported memory for the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue.
